Change c0465. Location: 1818 Vol. III, Ch. VI; 1831 Ch. XXIII.

Context before (unchanged): Cursed, cursed be the fiend that brought misery on his grey hairs, and doomed him to waste in wretchedness!

1818 text: He could not live under the horrors that were accumulated around him; an apoplectic fit was brought on, and in a few days he died in my arms.

1831 text: He could not live under the horrors that were accumulated around him; the springs of existence suddenly gave way: he was unable to rise from his bed, and in a few days he died in my arms.

Diff: He could not live under the horrors that were accumulated around him; [-an apoplectic fit-] {+the springs of existence suddenly gave way: he+} was [-brought on-] {+unable to rise from his bed+} , and in a few days he died in my arms.

Context after (unchanged): What then became of me?

result.rationale: Replaces the medical term 'an apoplectic fit was brought on' with the vaguer, more lyrical 'the springs of existence suddenly gave way: he was unable to rise from his bed.' Same event (Justine's... Victor's father dies), but the diction shifts from clinical cause to metaphorical collapse.
